title: Shifting Tone
text:
Writers choose their register with care, because a single word can change how a reader perceives the speaker. A formal report usually avoids contractions and prefers phrases such as 'it is recommended that'. In casual speech, by contrast, people say 'you should try it' and rely on everyday expressions that signal friendliness.

The boundary between these styles is not fixed. A conversational aside can soften an otherwise rigid argument, while an unexpectedly formal word in a friendly email may sound distant. Skilled communicators therefore adjust their register according to the relationship, the setting, and the purpose of the message.

Why might an unexpectedly formal word in a friendly email sound distant?
options: Because formal words are always rude
Because it mismatches the expected tone of the relationship

questions.text: What does the passage imply about skilled communicators?
options: They use one register for all situations
They adjust register to relationship, setting, and purpose

shortened forms of words, such as 'don't'
